title: The plan of a /prove-java-change run, as data
description: The plan of the retired proof run (llm-dlc/retired.md, proof-loop), kept as a format: verification/generated-observers/numbered_handoff.py and examples/tools/scaffold_example.py still write and read it. As that run used it: what stage 2 writes beside plan.md (llm-dlc/loop-summaries/prove-change/plan.json), and the setup and the proof loop read: the handoff from the review of the claims to the sessions that set them up and prove them (llm-dlc/runtime.md, stage 2). `watch.py plan --check` checks it; examples/tools/scaffold_example.py writes an example's designed claims and tasks from it.

request.description: The request, as the user gave it.

machine.description: Whether the machine is enough, what limits it, and the budget (doctor.py).

order.description: The examples' numbers, the most accessible first: the loop takes them in this order.

questions.description: What only the user can answer, each with the example it holds up.

numberFormat.description: The public parser's third argument. An explicit null uses its no-formatter path.

review.description: designed: stage 2 wrote the claims here (a catalog entry, a new change, or a correction); reviewed: claims already in the example, read again here; reused: claims unchanged since an accepted review (watch.py preflight's `reviewed`), not read again.

property.description: What the fix is meant to guarantee, in words: the property the claims state.

boundary.description: The preservation boundary: what the change may alter, and what it must leave as it was.

bounds.description: The bounds that make the claims meaningful, and why each is enough.

environment.description: Each assumption about the environment (locale, JDK, configuration, the code around the entry) the claims make.

claimFiles.description: Designed claims: each claim file's path in the example (claims/NAME.json) and its content, as examples/schema/target-claim.schema.json says.

tasks.description: Designed tasks, as the sidecar's tasks (examples/schema/target.schema.json): the proof tasks over the claims, and the replays.

remarks.description: On claims that exist: misstates (the claim says other than the example's own pages; setup corrects it, as the plan says) or suggestion (a claim to add or widen; the user's, and the example goes ahead as it stands).

controls.description: The controls the claims need: concrete inputs that must hold (positive), must fail (negative), and the constructed mutants that must fail the claim (mutation).

entry.description: How the proof is invoked: the method, the adapter if any, how inputs are built, and which of the three ways the setup expects to confirm.

gap.description: For a gap: the verifier's missing capability, as an engineering task.

preparedDeployments.description: Prepared ordered deployment manifests and JDK, relative to the plan. Stage 3 records the public entry bindings.

publicComparison.description: Materialize a numbered public comparison from its existing runtime and reviewed histories. Supply any missing semantic fixture values independently of the predictions.

preparation.description: The artifacts: how each revision is prepared and its dependency closure.

validation.description: The commands that check the setup, in order (validate_example.py --replay NNN at least).

approval.description: Whose word the claims were proved on: the decision `watch.py claims --accept` recorded.

closest.description: The closest past examples and what they cost.

hard.description: What the verifier may not model yet.

accessibility.description: Why it sits where it does in the order.
